summary: Cross-model history transform (new src/protocols/history.rs, pi transformMessages). Before every encode (explicit-route and legacy paths) and in Backend::validate_history_model, an assistant turn whose native_history names another wire, provider or model (requested_model for Claude) is replayed from its canonical text and tool calls: native_history and plain reasoning annotations are dropped (signatures, redacted thinking, encrypted Chat details, Gemini thoughtSignature parts), visible thinking (Claude thinking, Gemini thought parts, Chat reasoning text) is prepended to the turn text, and its tool-call IDs are rewritten into the target's limits ([A-Za-z0-9_-], 64; 40 for Chat) with the matching tool results renamed and uniqueness kept. Turns without an envelope keep their IDs unless the target would reject them outright (Anthropic). Turns the target owns are never touched: the transform returns None and the request is the recorded one. The old rejections ("opaque signed history cannot move to another model", provider/wire mismatch in validate_history_model, Chat reasoning cannot move) no longer fire for attributable foreign turns, so /model and connection switches are accepted. Gemini can now receive tool calls another model made (ID-less functionCall parts; Gemini 3 gets pi's skip_thought_signature_validator on the first call).

notes: A native_history envelope that does not name its wire/provider/model is not attributable and is left for the encoders to reject as before (the explicit-route opaque-history guards are unchanged). Integrity checks for history the target owns (Claude block/text agreement, Gemini parts digest, Chat reasoning digest) are unchanged. core.rs needed no change: set_model / select_connection / resume already go through Backend::validate_history_model. Context compaction (src/context.rs) still has its own opaque-history rule, which ZE-232 owns. No new non-test unwrap/expect/panic, unsafe or Arc<Mutex>; the transform clones the turn list only when it changes something.
